﻿# Radar


> Radar provides location infrastructure and intelligence to the Fortune 500 and high growth startups. From fighting fraud and optimizing operations to engaging customers at scale, Radar has the location layer that makes everything work better. By using real-time location and device signals, Radar helps brands meet their customers where they are, and create frictionless experiences. The core infrastructure falls into two groups: Geofencing and Maps. The geofencing platform lets you create circle, polygon, and isochrone geofences, and trigger events when people enter, exit, or dwell in a defined area. The maps platform is composed of search, geocoding, and routing APIs, as well as customizable base maps. Radar's solutions (Protect, Optimize, and Engage) are built on top of the infrastructure. Innovative businesses across verticals, like bet365, Foot Locker, Abercrombie & Fitch, Pizza Hut, RBC, and hundreds more, trust Radar.


## Products 


- [Geofencing](https://radar.com/product/geofencing): SDK for detecting when users enter or leave defined locations, built for high accuracy and battery efficiency. With Radar, you can create unlimited circle, polygon, and isochrone geofences. The meter-level accuracy is what separates Radar from competitors. With the platform, businesses can power every location moment, from engaging customers and tracking trips to running operations and detecting fraud.


- [Maps](https://radar.com/product/maps): Map tiles, styles, and APIs as an alternative to Google Maps and Mapbox. Radar Maps is trusted by hundreds of enterprises. Businesses looking for pinpoint accuracy at an affordable price tend to switch to Radar. With a suite of APIs and base maps that include classic, light, dark, and satellite styles, it has all the features you need to customize a user-friendly maps experience for your brand.


## Industries 


- [Retail](https://radar.com/industries/retail): Radar can power every moment in the customer journey, that's why retailers like DICK'S, Abercrombie & Fitch, and Victoria's Secret trust Radar. Whether you're sending location-based messages, detecting location spoofers for product releases, or creating in-store experiences, location is at the core of the customer experience. 


- [Financial Services](https://radar.com/industries/financial-services): Radar is trusted by financial services to drive traffic to partner merchants, stop fraud like account takeover, reduce friction at signup with address autocomplete, and build base maps that help users find branches.


- [Restaurants](https://radar.com/industries/restaurants): Restaurants that want to save on their maps bill, create engaging location-based experiences, and optimize their kitchen operations, switch to Radar. Dozens of enterprises like Inspire Brands, Pizza Hut, Panera, Dairy Queen, and more all use Radar to create better location-based experiences. This might mean a store locator that matches their brand, or sending location-based messages to drive incremental foot traffic and same-store sales.


- [Gaming](https://radar.com/industries/gaming): From geo-compliance to fraud prevention, Radar is the platform of choice for gaming operators ensuring they stay compliant. With Radar, you can verify every user is where they need to be, stop bad actors in their tracks, and even use maps APIs to onboard users faster at signup. Many of the top 10 operators, like bet365, trust Radar to power compliant gameplay across every market they operate in.


- [Travel](https://radar.com/industries/travel-and-hospitality): At the core of all travel experiences lies location. Whether a traveler is running to their gate for takeoff or checking into their hotel, location makes those experiences more frictionless and smoother. Leading airlines choose Radar to help customers find exactly where they need to go, reach them with relevant notifications, and provide customers with real-time location updates.


- [Logistics](https://radar.com/industries/logistics): Real-time location intelligence makes logistics operations run smoother. Whether you're tracking your workforce or monitoring delivery ETAs, Radar gives logistics teams like ShiftSmart and Taskrabbit complete visibility across every route, every worker, and shipment. Typically, logistics businesses choose Radar for satellite maps to visualize routes, workforce management for tracking teams, fraud detection to stop bad actors, and route optimization.


## Solutions


- [Protect](https://radar.com/solutions/protect): Radar Protect is a fraud detection and geo-compliance product that gives fraud and compliance teams real-time location and device signals to verify where a user physically is, not just who they claim to be. It works at the SDK level on iOS and Android, combining GPS, Wi-Fi, IP, Bluetooth, and sensor data into a single signal that is much harder to fake than IP geolocation, which a VPN or proxy can defeat. Teams use it to catch location spoofing and VPN use, detect account takeovers through signals like impossible travel and multi-device jumping, stop bonus and promo abuse from the same physical location or device across different user IDs, confirm physical presence for geo-compliance before a wager or transaction, and flag cloned devices, device farms, and emulators through environment fingerprinting.


- [Engage](https://radar.com/solutions/engage): Radar Engage is a location-based marketing and engagement product that gives marketing and product teams real-time location signals to reach a customer with the right message at the right moment. It collects location data through the standard Radar SDK, so there is nothing extra to install, then triggers push notifications or in-app messages when a user enters a geofence, visits a place, or reaches a high-intent location. Teams use it to send proximity-based offers while a customer is still deciding where to go, prompt loyalty redemptions and location-specific offers once someone is inside a store, and run competitor conquesting by detecting when a customer enters a rival location and reaching them with an offer. It can also build audience segments from real-world location history, including past visits, time spent at a place, and competitor visits. Engage works standalone or alongside an existing marketing stack like Braze, Airship, or Salesforce Marketing Cloud, firing location events those platforms use to trigger messages, and it can push events and segments into hundreds of marketing and analytics tools.


- [Optimize](https://radar.com/solutions/optimize): Radar Optimize is a location product for operations teams that handles pickup, delivery, workforce management, and fleet tracking. It tracks trips, workers, and vehicles in real time with high accuracy and battery efficiency, then uses real-time ETAs and arrival signals to automate workflows like order prep and automated check-in. Teams use it to catch anomalies such as no-shows, long wait times, and delays, and act before those problems reach the customer. Radar lets users build custom geofences, reports, and rules, and push or pull data between Radar and their own systems. The platform runs at large scale, processing billions of API calls a day from hundreds of millions of devices, and ships developer-friendly SDKs, documentation, and prebuilt integrations so teams can integrate quickly.

Every maps API your team needs
GEOCODING
Turn addresses into coordinates. And back again.

ADDRESS AUTOCOMPLETE
Help users find the right address on the first try

Explore address autocomplete →

Explore address validation →

Frequently asked questions
What industries and use cases is Radar Maps Platform built for?
Radar Maps Platform is built for product and engineering teams across verticals like retail, restaurants, logistics, financial services, travel, and gaming. Wherever location is part of the core user experience, Radar can be leveraged.
Does Radar Maps Platform support geocoding and reverse geocoding?
Yes. Radar Maps Platform includes forward geocoding, reverse geocoding, and IP geocoding APIs with global coverage.
What map styles does Radar offer?
Radar offers the following map styles:
Classic
: The default style with detailed street level info
Light
:
 
Light monochrome, useful for highlighting your own data
Dark
:
 
Dark monochrome, ideal for dark mode visualizations
Satellite
:
 
Provides global, high-resolution imagery for use cases that need it
Is Radar Maps Platform a good solution for enterprise apps?
Yes. Radar processes over 1 billion API calls per day from hundreds of millions of devices, with 99.99%+ API uptime. The platform is purpose-built for enterprise scale, with SOC 2 compliance, enterprise-grade privacy and security controls, and dedicated support.
‍
Teams building from scratch or switching from a legacy vendor can migrate in a single sprint. Customers like DICK'S Sporting Goods, Inspire Brands, and bet365 run location-critical workloads on Radar at scale.
Can I customize the map styling to match my brand?
Yes. Radar includes Maps Studio, a built-in style editor that lets you customize the look and feel of your maps without writing code. You can adjust colors, fonts, and layer visibility, directly in the dashboard.
